public_rationale: The study published January 16, 2024 reported GPT-4 pass@5 accuracy on CodeContests validation problems of 19% with a single-prompt method and 44% with AlphaCodium’s testing and revision workflow [e1]. AlphaCodium generated, ran and repaired code against public and AI-generated tests [e1]. These results support the concern about dependable correctness on the tested competitive-programming tasks, while also showing useful capability and improvement with testing and repair [e1].
limitations: The competitive-programming evaluation does not establish a representative success rate for everyday programming or direct control through English prompts [e1].
The assessment interprets 'works well' as dependable correctness; the evidence supplies no numerical threshold for satisfactory performance.
The December 2023 code-editing results fall outside the selected January 1–February 15, 2024 assessment period and provide context only [e2].

statement.document_title: The hottest new programming language is English! Or maybe not.

our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns dependable completion of English programming requests, not whether LLMs have any programming ability or usefulness.
Support requires substantial correctness or completion failures on clearly specified programming tasks. An occasional error alone would not establish the claim.
Because no reporting period is specified, assess early 2024: the latest completed calendar month and the elapsed portion of February before publication.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations show substantial failures to produce complete, correct programs from clear natural-language specifications, with testing or repair still necessary.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad evaluations of contemporaneous systems show dependable completion of varied programming requests without substantial correction, making the stated reliability concern unrepresentative.
